label: input token 2 (copy phase strongly; first two original positions weakly)
explanation: Token detector for the digit 2 as the current input. Strongest (about 0.7-0.98) when 2 is fed back during the copy phase, at any recall position; it peaks when 2 is the third copied token after two letters. In the original phase it fires only when 2 is at position 0 (about 0.40) or position 1 (weaker, about 0.2); a 2 at original position 2 or later almost never fires it (t=2 occasionally about 0.13). About 88% of activation mass is in the copy phase. It does not fire on the delimiter or on other digits. A few weak spurious activations occur on letters (n, e, k) just before a copied 2. Dev: P=0.99, R=0.95, F1=0.97, mass recall 0.99.

issues: The main claims hold. in_tok==2 & phase==2 has precision 1.00 and gives 70% of recall. 2 at t=0 has precision 1.00 (constant at about 0.40). 2 at t>=3 in the original phase has precision 0.0004. 2 at t=2 has precision 0.055, so it fires only rarely, as the explanation says. Test scores reproduce: P 0.991, R 0.955, F1 0.973, mass recall 0.991.

One systematic false-positive class was not mentioned. A 2 at t=1 never fires when the token at t=0 was also 2 (prev_tok==2: 546 dev steps, precision 0.0). That is about half of all false positives. When prev_tok != 2, a 2 at t=1 has precision 0.966. The class is small, and excluding it raises test precision only from 0.991 to 0.995 (F1 0.973 to 0.975).

Wrong detail: the explanation says the weak letter activations come 'just before a copied 2'. Scoring non-2 inputs in the copy phase with next_out==2 gives precision 0.0005 and recall 0.0003, so that is not where they are. The non-2 activations (about 3.8% of active steps, under 1% of mass) gather at recall_idx==1, the first copied token right after <DEL>. They are weak noise and do not change the label.
